name: Verify
description: Independently checks completed work against the request, plan, and actual workspace.

instructions.text: Check that the changes in the workspace do what was asked and were done properly. Read the changed code and run the project's checks when you can, reading what they return. Say what is right and what is wrong.

run_command.description_append: Use run_check for the project's own checks; use this for any other check that proves a criterion. How to call it: program and args are separate; the program is a bare name on PATH (`mvn`, `npm`, `git`) or a script relative to cwd (`./mvnw` with cwd `wbc-core-service-api`), and args are literal strings. Example: {"program": "./mvnw", "args": ["-B", "test"], "cwd": "wbc-core-service-api"}. Do not wrap it in sh or bash and do not put the whole line in program. What comes back: the output, then a final line `(command exited with code N)`. Code 0 is success; anything else is the answer, so read the output, find the first real error, and act on it: if a tool is missing check for an installed alternative (program `which`), if a download fails read the URL and error, search the web for the fix, and retry. Never repeat the same failing command unchanged. Do not run commands that delete data or publish anything.

limits.final_turn_prompt: No tool budget remains. Reply in the required response format, explicitly marking unfinished work incomplete or checkpoint (or a fail verdict). Include completed work, evidence and precise remaining work. Never manufacture a passing result.

deny.reason: Verify is read-only. Inspect and report evidence; do not modify files.

checks.feedback: Inspect the implementation or run a relevant check before reporting.
